name: Jehu
bio:
Jehu son of Nimshi is first named at Horeb, where the LORD instructed Elijah to anoint him king over Israel (1 Kings 19:16) — one of three anointings Elijah was told to carry out, alongside Hazael as king over Syria and Elisha as prophet in his own place. The LORD declared that whoever escaped Hazael's sword, Jehu would slay, and whoever escaped Jehu's sword, Elisha would slay, marking Jehu as an instrument of judgment against the house of Ahab and against Baal worship in Israel (1 Kings 19:15-18).

## 📖 Core Story: Anointed, and the Blood of Ahab's House

Elisha sent a young prophet to Ramoth Gilead to anoint Jehu, a military captain, king over Israel in secret, with orders to flee immediately after. The young man found Jehu among the army commanders, poured oil on his head, and delivered the LORD's charge: Jehu was to destroy the house of Ahab in vengeance for the prophets' blood and Jezebel's crimes, so that Ahab's entire dynasty would perish like Jeroboam's and Baasha's, and dogs would eat Jezebel at Jezreel. Jehu's fellow officers, once they heard, immediately proclaimed him king, spreading garments under him and blowing trumpets (2 Kings 9:1-13).

Jehu rode to Jezreel, where Jehoram (Joram), king of Israel, lay recovering from wounds, with Ahaziah, king of Judah, visiting him. When Jehoram's messengers asked whether Jehu came in peace, Jehu told each to fall in behind him instead of answering. Jehoram himself rode out and asked the same question; Jehu answered, "What peace, so long as the whoredoms of thy mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts are so many?" As Jehoram fled, Jehu shot him through the heart with a full-strength arrow, killing him, and had his body thrown into Naboth's field in direct fulfillment of Elijah's old curse on Ahab. Jehu then pursued Ahaziah and had him struck down in his chariot as well; Ahaziah fled wounded to Megiddo and died there (2 Kings 9:14-28).

Arriving at Jezreel, Jehu found Jezebel defiantly watching from a window, taunting him by name as another king's assassin. Jehu called for anyone loyal to him to throw her down, and the eunuchs did; her blood splattered the wall and the horses trampled her body. Jehu ordered her buried out of respect for her royal blood, but by then dogs had eaten all but her skull, feet, and palms — exactly as Elijah had prophesied years before (2 Kings 9:30-37).

## 📖 Core Story: Purging Ahab's House and Baal Worship

Jehu wrote to Samaria's officials challenging them to crown one of Ahab's seventy sons and fight him if they dared; terrified, they instead beheaded all seventy and sent the heads to Jezreel in baskets. Jehu displayed them in two heaps at the city gate and declared to the gathered people that the LORD's word against Ahab's house, spoken through Elijah, had now been completely fulfilled. He went on to kill everyone remaining of Ahab's household, officials, close friends, and priests in Jezreel, leaving none alive (2 Kings 10:1-11). On the road to Samaria, he also intercepted and killed forty-two relatives of Ahaziah, king of Judah (2 Kings 10:12-14).

Jehu met Jehonadab son of Rechab on the road, asked if his heart was aligned with Jehu's own, and took him into his chariot to witness his zeal for the LORD. In Samaria, he killed everyone left of Ahab's line. He then announced a great sacrifice to Baal, secretly to lure out and destroy Baal's worshippers rather than genuinely honor the god. Every worshipper of Baal in Israel assembled in Baal's temple, and once they were inside offering sacrifices, Jehu had his guards slaughter them all, destroyed Baal's idols, tore down his temple, and turned the site into a latrine — wiping out Baal worship from Israel (2 Kings 10:15-28).

Jehu never abandoned the golden calves of Jeroboam at Bethel and Dan, however, so the LORD, while commending his obedience in destroying Ahab's house and promising his descendants four generations on Israel's throne, noted that Jehu did not follow the LORD's law wholeheartedly. In his days the LORD began to let Israel's territory shrink, as Hazael struck Israelite land east of the Jordan. Jehu reigned twenty-eight years and was buried in Samaria; his son Jehoahaz succeeded him (2 Kings 10:29-36).
